# repair

`repair` implements REPAIR: structural regression involving random coefficients
from a Gaussian mixed model, with a modified method-of-moments correction for
sampling error in the estimated coefficients. It uses **likelihood-only scores**
and their sampling-error covariance, rather than treating shrunken BLUPs as
error-free observed variables.

This is a development package. The supported structural workflow is an additive
regression with an intercept, using random coefficients from **one fitted
`lme4::lmer()` or linear `nlme::lme()` model with one grouping factor**. Random coefficients may be
predictors, the outcome, or both. Numeric, logical, and factor observed predictors
are supported. See the [workflow guide](vignettes/repair-workflow.Rmd) for matching,
omission, interpretation, and current limits.

## Install

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("zacharyvig/repair")
```

Installation from source requires R >= 4.3 and a C++20 compiler with the R build
toolchain. On Windows, use the Rtools version appropriate for your R installation.

## Fit, inspect, and summarize

Fit the measurement model using its usual `lmer()` or `lme()` interface. Its weights,
offsets, contrasts, estimation choices, and effective observations remain under
your control. Supply structural variables in a separate data frame containing
one row per analysis ID.

```{r example}
library(repair)
growth <- lme4::lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), lme4::sleepstudy)

# Illustrative person-level predictor, not an actual sleepstudy measurement.
people <- data.frame(
  Subject = levels(lme4::sleepstudy$Subject),
  observed = seq_len(18)
)

repair_effects(list(growth = growth))
fit <- repair(
  re("Days", model = "growth") ~ observed,
  models = list(growth = growth),
  data = people,
  id = "Subject"
)
summary(fit)
```

The marker `re("Days", model = "growth")` selects the random slope for `Days`.
It represents a deviation from the fitted fixed slope. Use
`re("(Intercept)", model = "growth")` for the random intercept. When there is
only one matching effect, `model` may be omitted.

```{r accessors}
coef(fit)
confint(fit)
nobs(fit)  # people, not repeated observations
```

## Inspect what enters the estimator

```{r inspection}
analysis <- repair_data(
  re("Days", model = "growth") ~ observed,
  models = list(growth = growth), data = people, id = "Subject"
)
analysis
head(analysis@ids)
head(analysis@predictors)
analysis@diagnostics$excluded
```

IDs determine alignment; data-frame row order never determines a match. The
person-level data frame defines the requested cohort. Missing/nonfinite values,
unmatched IDs, and failed scores stop by default. Use `na_action = "omit"` to
explicitly exclude them with a warning and an ID/reason audit trail.

`fit@analysis_data` retains the matched scores, error covariance, selected effect
sources, and exclusions. `fit@struc_fit` retains M-MOM steps and numerical
diagnostics. For custom score/error inputs, use the lower-level `fit_mmom()` API.

## Interpretation and limits

- Standard errors are model-based and conditional on estimated measurement-model
  quantities. They use the modified final predictor moment, consistent with the
  manuscript and primary simulation estimator. Measurement-model parameter
  uncertainty is not propagated; intervals and tests use a normal reference.
- `regularization = "minimum"` is the default. `"none"` disables stabilization
  but **still corrects for measurement error**. Custom settings require `alpha`.
- Observed structural variables are assumed measured without error. The complete
  error covariance is preserved when random coefficients appear on both sides.
- Interactions or nonlinear transformations involving random coefficients,
  models without an intercept, joint multiple-equation fitting, and cross-model
  error covariances are not implemented. Unsupported formulas fail explicitly.
- Single-group `nlme` models support independent/AR(1)/continuous-time AR(1)
  correlation and constant/`varIdent`/`varPower` residual variance. Keep the data
  in the fit (`keep.data = TRUE`). See the [nlme reproduction guide](vignettes/nlme-workflow.Rmd).
- Multi-group lme4 scoring remains experimental; multi-group structural fits and
  multilevel nlme extraction are rejected. Shared nuisance effects can create
  cross-person score errors that the structural estimator cannot represent.

## Development and reproducibility

The [design plan](dev/package_plan.Rmd) describes the implemented contracts and
extension sequence. The [audit and decisions](dev/design-audit.md) trace findings
to corrections and tests. The test suite includes frozen REPAIR simulation and
independent algebra-audit fixtures for both R and C++ backends, plus three
end-to-end nlme reproduction datasets; see
[fixture provenance](tests/testthat/fixtures/README.md).

```r
# From a source checkout:
testthat::test_local()
```
